thread.title: Unity Rules Engine Development
thread.preview:
That fits the adopted policy. **Sparse advancement is an engineering optimization, not a different clock or refresh rule.**

Preserve these invariants:

- Derive the current interval and next boundary from exact time and the original schedule. Skipped intervals grant no banked Actions, movement or Reactions.
- Collapse only boundaries whose consequences are provably equivalent. Preserve expired stance/Press state and current allowances without fabricating historical commands or receipts.
- Stop at meaningful life, effect, job and traversal events. During running, a Start requires settling prior-interval travel, resolving Start effects, then paying the next legal Dash before further travel.
- Preserve boundary processing identity across save/load. A cursor must distinguish “arrived at this timestamp” from “already resolved its ordered events.”
- Remote work earns only its actual compatible labor; skipping empty combat markers neither pauses it nor awards additional work.

Validate sparse advancement against ordinary sequential advancement over manageable spans, including exact-boundary entry, shortened bootstrap intervals, dying actors, expiring conditions, interrupted running and save/resume. Long idle farming spans should then produce the same observable state without generating every empty Start.

The **797-case checkpoint remains structural/history evidence** until the connected runtime and those behaviors are exercised.

Sparse skipping must preserve latest real interval identity, no banked allowances, and must stop at meaningful life/effect/traversal markers. Current 797-case history prerequisites remain schema13 structural only, no shared-world runtime claimed yet.

content.text: Agree/adopt your written 2cb0a559-db85-5535-ab07-45c2b5d3321b NEW completions under owner's delegation: resolved predicate, finish outgoing slot/no remaining-round award, fixed virtual schedule survives control-mode exit/reentry, preserved interval spending, outside life markers, exact partial cardinal travel, actor-specific job pause/no auto-resume. Main independent prerequisite now passing795 cases: strict canonical mixed command replay and structural archive schema13. Archive is for genuinely closed identities, NOT a license to restart the continuing fixed encounter; shared host must keep its schedule while mode changes. Head now a50024de remotely (your bb391 cached). One remaining pre-first-encounter detail: exploration starts with no established regular schedule. For walking/running action/interval budgets, recommend per-actor six-second activity intervals anchored at world start, then preserve already-spent allowances when allocating first tactical schedule? Need exact first-entry policy so precombat running cannot grant a free second Dash/action. Also confirm virtual Start outside tactical expires stance/Press and refreshes ordinary allowances without auto-selecting any stance; exploration has no mandatory stance until tactical relevant event. I will implement other agreed portions meanwhile.

items.text:
**Recommend establishing the fixed virtual schedule at shared-world creation**, using the approved equal-slot allocator for this fixture’s explicitly supplied, fixed initiative order. First tactical entry then changes control mode without allocating another Action, Dash, movement budget or Reaction.

I’m using your latest receipt’s adopted transition policy: **finish the outgoing slot, award no remaining round, preserve the schedule and interval spending**.

The source basis is:

- [Combat: encounter resources and timing, lines 29–66](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md#L29): ordinary turn allowances, initial Reaction, own-Start refresh, preserved effect markers and ordered Start/End processing.
- [Expedition FL-01/03](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/expedition/EXPEDITION_PLAYER_BOOK.md#L28): expedition activity grants no second allowance; initiative does not reset elapsed time.
- [Approved initial allocation](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/docs/unity/PROTOTYPE_RULE_DECISIONS.md#L118): equal slots and outgoing-before-incoming ordering. **Moving that allocation to world creation is a NEW completion**, not something that receipt already decided.

Use this exact **NEW provisional completion** for the bounded shared host:

| Boundary | Contract |
|---|---|
| World creation | Persist one schedule ID, world origin `W`, and the fixture’s established order of `N` actors. Actor `i` has Starts at `W + 6i/N + 6k`, and Ends one slot-width later. Do not fabricate pre-origin turns or events. |
| Initial allowances | Initialize each actor’s ordinary allowance once at `W`. Process actor 0’s origin Start once. Other actors have a deliberately shortened initial interval ending at their first scheduled Start; that Start refreshes normally. No proportional allowance or retroactive work. |
| Exploration | Charge walking expenditure and paid Dash to that actor’s current interval. Changing input, pausing, saving or switching modes preserves the ledger. |
| First tactical entry | Keep the existing schedule, cursor, marker-processing state and spending. Enter the slot containing the current timestamp; do not replay its Start. Its eventual End remains at its original timestamp. |
| Entry exactly at a boundary | Resolve the outgoing End and incoming Start once, in the approved order, before voluntary tactical input. Entry supplies no additional refresh. |
| Subsequent mode changes | Preserve the same schedule and encounter identity while that encounter continues. A partial first tactical round advances only its remaining scheduled time; complete rounds remain six seconds. |

**Bootstrap consequence:** a later actor can spend its initial allowance and refresh at its first scheduled Start less than six seconds after world creation. That is intentional and explicit—not a rolling six-second cooldown. A mode change never causes that refresh.

For example, with two actors, A’s Starts are `0, 6, 12…`, B’s are `3, 9, 15…`. If A pays Dash while exploring at `t=1`, tactical entry at `t=2` leaves A’s Action spent and movement expenditure intact. A cannot receive another ordinary Action until `t=6`. B’s legitimate `t=3` refresh remains unchanged.

For this fixture, treat the initialized Reaction as its **single initial allowance**, rather than granting it again on first tactical entry. Extending initialization before combat is part of this NEW policy; the source itself phrases initialization as “begin an encounter.” This does not decide genuine later encounters or roster changes.

**Yes: outside tactical mode, the established virtual Start expires stance/Press and refreshes ordinary interval allowances, without automatically selecting a stance.** Distinguish the authorities:

- Expiry at the captured next regular Start is source-backed: [Stances](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md#L113) and [Press](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md#L148).
- Using those outside Starts to refresh ordinary activity budgets is the **adopted shared-host completion**, not a consequence inferred solely from the source’s duration-preservation rule.
- **NEW stance completion:** exploration requires no selection. An existing stance remains operative until its real expiry. During an actor’s active tactical regular slot, require selection before its first applicable voluntary event—or before End if capable and no such event occurs. No off-turn selection, automatic stance or retroactive benefit.

At a Start crossed during running, reset the ordinary movement/Dash ledger normally. Continuing doubled pace must pay a fresh legal Dash. A persisted run instruction may authorize that payment; if payment becomes illegal, suspend traversal at the boundary rather than silently granting speed or switching to walking.

Keep these constraints:

- The supplied order concerns the **fixed encounter roster**, not every expedition member. [FL-16](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/expedition/EXPEDITION_PLAYER_BOOK.md#L327) still separates participants from remote companions. Their compatible work continues on shared elapsed time.
- Virtual Starts are processing checkpoints, not exclusive exploration work windows or six-second job rewards.
- Use globally unique schedule-marker identities for life processing. These actors already have a schedule, so outside dying uses its next eligible Start; do not add a competing onset-plus-six timer.
- Merely establishing this calendar does **not** change outside-initiative bare-duration rules: those effects still receive their sourced absolute deadlines.
- Preserve [FL-15’s continuing retreat/pursuit identity](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/expedition/EXPEDITION_PLAYER_BOOK.md#L307). Calendar creation is not encounter creation, closure or permission to archive a continuing encounter.

The alternative—separate exploration intervals followed by tactical allocation—requires an additional handoff rule reconciling two refresh calendars. The fixed schedule avoids that extra policy within your current fixed-roster scope.

I'm reading those now; preserve that ongoing encounter for retreat/pursuit rather than treat a UI return as a fresh encounter/resource refill. LastDeathTurn currently ordinal+1 must become globally unique across genuine new encounters. Future worker reservations need pause/reconciliation, and remote companions shouldn't globally stop. Please include these actual sources in disposition and give the smallest exact provisional gap completions, rather than accept my earlier proposed anti-reset timestamp if source provides a better contract.

items.text:
**Recommend one shared-world profile with persistent clocks, explicit mode transitions, and exact partial movement.** Keep the fixed roster/order for this increment; changing modes must not reconstruct actors, inventories, jobs or resources.

Public Engine HEAD remains `bb391e4d`; I’m treating schema12’s completion as your reported local status.

The sources establish much of the continuity, but **ordinary victory exit timing, outside-combat death-save scheduling, and movement interrupted between cells need explicit provisional completions**.

1. **Encounter exit and reentry**

   **Sourced:** combat concludes through actual surrender, capture, pursuit and other consequences—not merely winning initiative. Existing effect markers survive leaving/reentering initiative. Expedition retreat explicitly preserves the encounter, spent resources and actual survivors; it is not a free mode toggle. See [Combat: encounter resources and timing](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/bb391e4d4b6c2d1ee4b1c1103008065308acb8e2/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md#L27-L68) and [Expedition FL-15](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/bb391e4d4b6c2d1ee4b1c1103008065308acb8e2/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/expedition/EXPEDITION_PLAYER_BOOK.md#L306-L324).

   **NEW recommended completion for this fixed-roster world:**

   - Exit requires an authoritative **resolved-conflict predicate**. Initially support all required hostile actors Dead, or a specifically authored resolution event. Temporary Unconscious, paralysis, invisibility or inability to reach the player is insufficient.
   - Require all attacks, knockout choices, OA windows and Press continuations to finish.
   - **Complete the outgoing slot, not the remaining round.** Advance only to its recorded End, processing intervening world deadlines and that End’s consequences. Revalidate the exit predicate there.
   - If an intervening event reopens conflict or requires a decision, stop closure there. Preserve already-resolved time and consequences.
   - Exit changes control mode after outgoing End. It grants no healing, resource refresh, new stance, fresh movement budget or reward.
   - Keep the fixed roster’s six-second virtual schedule running in exploration. Reentry resumes that schedule and the applicable slot/interval; it does not execute another initial encounter setup or duplicate a previously processed Start.

   This last point is a **new resource-continuity policy**, extending the sourced virtual-marker model. Preserve Action, interaction, movement/Dash, Reaction, Mobile and Press expenditure until their actual scheduled refresh/expiry. Exploration expenditure must also be recorded where it uses those resources. Never replay unused virtual turns as available actions.

   Stances and armed Press retain their captured next-Start expiry; Disengage retains its actual turn-End expiry. Do not clear or extend them merely because the mode changed. If exploration would produce an eligible OA/Press event, enter tactical resolution **before that departure**, using the preserved state.

   First encounter allocation remains the adopted equal-slot procedure. Arbitrary new rosters/reordering remain separate from this fixed-roster continuation. Changing a mode or encounter ID cannot manufacture a fresh encounter-use allowance.

2. **Dying outside tactical control**

   **Sourced:** death saves occur at regular Starts; Stable recovery has an absolute deadline; the expedition rules explicitly retain life procedures during travel and work. Healing-pulse rules provide a precedent for continuing original six-second virtual schedules outside initiative. See [Core life rules](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/bb391e4d4b6c2d1ee4b1c1103008065308acb8e2/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md#L50-L60), [Expedition FL-01](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/bb391e4d4b6c2d1ee4b1c1103008065308acb8e2/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/expedition/EXPEDITION_PLAYER_BOOK.md#L28-L34), and [Healing pulses: timing](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/bb391e4d4b6c2d1ee4b1c1103008065308acb8e2/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/HEALING_PULSE_PLAYTEST.md#L9-L13).

   I did **not** find a complete explicit outside-combat death-save schedule.

   **NEW completion:** continue death saves at the actor’s preserved virtual regular Starts, exactly once per marker. Exit, pause, save/load and reentry cannot postpone or duplicate them. Stable/Dead creatures skip them normally.

   If dying first begins without any established regular schedule, set the first life marker to **onset + six seconds**, then every six seconds. Preserve that cadence across entry rather than adding a second series of death saves.

   At a due life marker, retain expiry → permitted absolute recovery → death save → ordinary later healing ordering. For the new outside-initiative scheduler, explicitly place this life-processing block before ordinary rest/treatment completion; this is a **new cross-system ordering completion**, not wording recovered from FL-03. Preserve FL-03’s other relative priorities and the adopted crop-local exceptions.

3. **Direct exploration movement**

   **Already adopted:** ordinary walking pace is supplied walking Speed divided by six; running uses paid Dash at twice that pace. Combat terrain costs, condition restrictions and the same world geometry remain applicable. See [prototype traversal policy](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/bb391e4d4b6c2d1ee4b1c1103008065308acb8e2/docs/unity/PROTOTYPE_RULE_DECISIONS.md#L42-L54).

   For constant Speed \(S>0\), distance \(d\), movement-cost multiplier \(c\), and pace factor \(p\) of 1 walking or 2 running:

   \[
   \Delta t=\frac{6dc}{pS}
   \]

   Here \(c\) includes the strongest terrain multiplier plus applicable crawl/squeeze additions. Running requires current Dash permission; Dazed does not gain running merely because time is real-time.

   **NEW execution completion:**

   - Start with validated level-ground cardinal edges between the existing five-foot cells.
   - Persist exact rational progress along the current edge as actual position—not merely an animation or reservation.
   - Advance only to the earliest route endpoint, world deadline, resource boundary or interruption.
   - Credit actual elapsed travel and distance up to that instant, process the event, then recompute legality and pace.
   - Never finish a whole cell early, discard partial distance, refund elapsed time, or snap the actor to either endpoint.

   Example: Speed30, normal ground: a five-foot walk takes one second. A deadline after 0.4 seconds finds the actor **two feet along the edge**. Becoming immobile stops there; a Speed change alters only subsequent travel.

   Retained interval budgets can also stop movement: exiting tactical mode does not bypass already-spent movement. Sustained running needs a newly paid Dash at subsequent applicable intervals.

   **Narrow geometry gate:** the first encounter triggers may occur only at authored grid-aligned locations, where the tactical geometry is defined. An unsupported mid-edge encounter must stop explicitly at the actual position; it cannot silently snap or ignore the threat. Partial movement itself remains implemented and persisted.

4. **Workers, interruption and reservations**

   [FL-02/03](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/bb391e4d4b6c2d1ee4b1c1103008065308acb8e2/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/expedition/EXPEDITION_PLAYER_BOOK.md#L37-L62) and [EC-02](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/bb391e4d4b6c2d1ee4b1c1103008065308acb8e2/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/expedition/EX58_SOURCE_CONTRACTS_CORRECTED.md#L48-L69) require actual compatible work, location/access and reservations. Feasible progress survives interruption unless the particular procedure says otherwise.

   Credit the valid interval **before** the interruption, then apply the job’s own disposition:

   | Procedure | Required interruption behavior |
   |---|---|
   | Camp Greens labor | Retain completed labor and spent inputs. Stop unavailable work; keep crop growth/care/failure/freshness clocks running. Release unused worker bookings. |
   | Ordinary intake | Preserve consumed credit; release untouched reserved stock. Combat entry interrupts intake under the adopted profile. |
   | Stable supported filling | Pause with completed labor and source/capacity reservations retained; release future worker/hand bookings; transfer nothing before completion. |
   | Cancellation | Use that procedure’s cancellation rules; do not substitute cancellation for every interruption. |

   **NEW connected-host completion:** entering tactical participation pauses that actor’s incompatible crop/filling work using the dispositions above. Ending the condition or encounter does not automatically resume work; resume explicitly after revalidating capability, location, tools and reservations.

   Independent companions may continue compatible work outside the encounter. Tactical decision pause still pauses the whole shared simulation. Conditions are evaluated against each task’s actual requirements—not a blanket “any condition stops all work.”

   For filling, retain the supported stationary arrangement. Spills, breakage or a dropped actively handled vessel remain unsupported until their physical outcomes are defined; reservations never make an object immune to those events.

5. **Next coherent implementation**

   Build one explicit shared-world snapshot profile containing the existing world, inventory, jobs, life, conditions, tactical state and movement continuation. Compose the existing procedures behind one authoritative dispatcher rather than nesting their separate fixture initialization paths.

   The first acceptance scenario should demonstrate:

   - Direct movement to an authored encounter trigger.
   - Combat while a separate companion’s compatible assignment shares elapsed time.
   - Exit at outgoing End without resource or deadline resets.
   - Movement back to the plot; harvest, pickup/transfer and actual intake using existing rules.
   - Continued exploration with the resulting inventory, health, job and condition state.
   - Save/resume during partial movement and at a mode boundary, producing the same results.

   Keep these new transition policies explicitly provisional. The narrow gates are changed rosters, unsupported off-grid combat, hazardous vessel outcomes and unsupplied job capabilities—not the entire connected loop.

**Agree with encounter history keyed by encounter ID, separate from the active encounter pointer. Use encounter identity—not a new cooldown timestamp—to prevent mode-toggle refills.**

The sources support that distinction. I checked current Engine `a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e`.

1. **Immediate resolved-conflict exit — NEW provisional completion**

   Agree: commit exit at the **current, already-resolved timestamp**, provided the authoritative conflict-resolution predicate is satisfied and no attack, knockout, OA or Press continuation remains pending.

   Do not add an unplayed slot or round, manufacture an End event, or advance incoming turns. Record the current turn as **closed by encounter resolution**, with its actual expenditure and timestamp—not as an ordinarily completed turn.

   Existing registered absolute deadlines, virtual endpoints and source-triggered consequences remain scheduled. Exit itself neither expires nor refreshes them.

   **This replaces my earlier proposed outgoing-slot completion.** That proposal was not a recovered source rule. Likewise, do not automatically run the old encounter’s entire resource-refresh calendar outside combat merely because effect markers continue.

2. **Retreat/pursuit is continuation, not a fresh encounter — sourced**

   [FL-15, lines 307–324](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/expedition/EXPEDITION_PLAYER_BOOK.md#L307-L324) explicitly preserves the encounter, numbered rounds, positions, conditions, pursuit actors and spent resources. Successful retreat returns to Expedition Mode without refreshing RP, recharge or encounter-use resources.

   Therefore:

   - A UI/control-mode change does not close the underlying conflict.
   - Retreat uses its actual round procedure and consequences; it cannot use the zero-time resolved-conflict exit above.
   - Preserve a resumable encounter reference even when no tactical encounter is currently presented.
   - Recontact during that ongoing retreat/pursuit resumes the existing encounter. A new UUID alone cannot authorize initialization.

   If FL-15 execution is not implemented yet, gate **Retreat**, while allowing the independently defined resolved-conflict exit.

3. **Refresh eligibility across encounters — source-first contract**

   [COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST §Encounter and action resources](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md#L27-L41) expressly supplies an initial encounter Reaction and refreshes at regular own-turn Starts.

   | Event | Resource treatment |
   |---|---|
   | Exit or UI mode change | No refresh. |
   | Resume the same encounter | Preserve spending; do not repeat initial grants or an already-processed Start. |
   | Actual later regular own-turn Start | Apply that Start’s sourced grants once. |
   | Genuinely new encounter | Apply its sourced initial Reaction rule, subject to prohibitions; ordinary turn budgets arise through its actual turns. |
   | New encounter ID without a new encounter | Reject initialization. |

   **Do not adopt `nextEligibleRegularStart` as a universal cooldown.** It would restrict genuine new encounters beyond the inspected source. A genuine new encounter’s initial Reaction is a legitimate grant, distinct from refilling through a presentation toggle.

   **NEW identity completion:** require a trusted world/scenario event establishing the new conflict, linked to the previous encounter’s disposition where relevant. The same unresolved threat cannot repeatedly mint “new encounters.” For the bounded fixture, enumerate these entry/resolution events explicitly.

   No blanket reset of RP, charges, recharge clocks or other resources follows; each requires its own source rule.

4. **Carry existing effects through a genuinely new encounter**

   The [virtual-marker rule](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md#L45-L53) preserves their original deadlines. New encounter initialization must not overwrite an old stance, Press record or other still-running effect.

   **NEW narrow overlap completion:** an existing stance and its spent finite allowances remain effective until their captured endpoint; an earlier new-encounter Start does not replace/replenish that stance. Likewise, preserve the existing Press interval and its consumed/unconsumed disposition until its captured endpoint. After expiry, ordinary selection/arming requires the usual eligible own-turn opportunity.

   This resolves the overlapping-effect case without imposing a global Reaction cooldown.

5. **Outside-combat death saves — NEW scheduling completion**

   [FL-01](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/expedition/EXPEDITION_PLAYER_BOOK.md#L28-L34) retains regular-Start death saves during expedition procedures. [Healing-pulse timing](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/HEALING_PULSE_PLAYTEST.md#L9-L13) provides virtual-clock precedent, but does not itself specify death-save scheduling.

   Adopt:

   - An actor with an established schedule retains its six-second Start markers for dying processing outside combat.
   - Without an established schedule, newly dying outside combat creates its first marker at **onset + six seconds**, then every six seconds.
   - An already-running dying schedule survives entry/reentry unchanged. A newly assigned encounter Start does not create an additional competing save.
   - Stable, positive-HP and Dead states skip saves normally. Stable recovery retains its original absolute deadline.

   Replace encounter-local `ordinal + 1` identity with a globally unique marker identity, such as **schedule ID + actor ID + marker index**, plus ordering where needed. Replaying the same marker never rolls again. A new dying episode must not make an already-processed marker reusable.

6. **Workers and reservations — sourced separation**

   [FL-16](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/expedition/EXPEDITION_PLAYER_BOOK.md#L327-L331) distinguishes expedition membership from encounter participation. [FL-02/03](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/expedition/EXPEDITION_PLAYER_BOOK.md#L49-L62) and [EC-02](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/a50024de12b855d490097de35a00abf7b05f812e/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/expedition/EX58_SOURCE_CONTRACTS_CORRECTED.md#L48-L69) require actual compatible intervals.

   Pause/reconcile incompatible work for actual participants and affected workers. Preserve earned progress and apply each job’s reservation/interruption rules. Remote compatible workers continue when shared time advances; tactical decision pause still pauses everyone. Specific adopted job-entry rules remain controlling.

These are sufficient to proceed with independent encounter histories and the first connected-world transition. Record the immediate-exit, encounter-identity, effect-overlap and outside-death-save completions explicitly as provisional consensus policy.
